column3: The Hebrew begins with singular “the commandment” and does not explicitly name the person commanded to teach; BSB has plural “the commandments” and supplies “me.”
The Hebrew has singular “your son” and “your son’s son”; BSB has plural “your children and grandchildren.”

The Hebrew has singular “your heart”; BSB has plural “your hearts.”
The Hebrew uses a verb whose literal image is sharpening the words for the children; BSB expresses this as teaching them diligently.
The Hebrew has singular “a sign” and “your hand,” and places the frontlets “between your eyes”; BSB has plural “reminders,” “hands,” and “on your foreheads.”
The Hebrew has singular “your house”; BSB has plural “your houses.”
